question.text: An electron moves through a uniform magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. At a particular instant of time, the velocity of electron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>u</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the magnetic force acting on electron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>e</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>e</mi></math> is the charge of electron, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is ____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Force acting on a charged particle under the magnetic field is given by, F→=qv→×B→.

⇒5ek⏜=e3i⏜+5j⏜×B0i⏜+2B0j⏜

⇒5ek⏜=e6B0k⏜-5B0k⏜

⇒B0=5 T
